sections.h2: Where is South Jordan, Utah, and how large is it?
sections.html:
South Jordan is a Salt Lake County city in the south-central part of the Salt Lake Valley, about 18 miles south of Salt Lake City. Wikipedia lists its area at roughly 22 square miles, with the Jordan River on the low side near 4,300 feet and the Oquirrh foothills climbing to about 5,200 feet on the west.

The 2020 Census counted 77,487 residents, up from 50,418 in 2010. Growth of that size means a large share of the housing stock was built in recent decades, so roof age and finished-basement permits come up often.

The whole city sits inside one county, so a South Jordan seller deals with the Salt Lake County Assessor, Treasurer and Recorder, and with one school district, Jordan School District.

sections.h2: How did South Jordan grow from a farm settlement into Daybreak?
sections.html:
South Jordan began with Alexander Beckstead, who became the first settler in 1859. A church branch organized in 1863 gave the community its name, and voters approved incorporation on November 8, 1935.

The biggest change came in 2004, when Kennecott Land began Daybreak, a master-planned community of about 4,200 acres on the west side. The remaining 1,300 undeveloped acres were sold to Larry H. Miller Group in 2022, and a new Downtown Daybreak opened in 2025 with the Salt Lake Bees ballpark as its anchor.

The city's own FAQ says Downtown Daybreak sits inside a Housing Transit Reinvestment Zone along the Mountain View Corridor, between two existing TRAX stations. The city expects the project to add housing and transit use in what it calls the fastest-growing quadrant of Salt Lake County. For a seller on the west side, that means more construction nearby for several more years.

sections.h2: What do the official numbers say about South Jordan housing?
sections.html:
Census QuickFacts describes a high-income, owner-heavy city with larger households than most of the valley. The figures below are the Census Bureau's 2020 to 2024 estimates unless noted.

MeasureSouth Jordan
2020 Census population77,487
Owner-occupied housing rate81.4%
Median value of owner-occupied homes$650,500
Median gross rent$1,991
Persons per household3.09
Median household income$134,047
Mean travel time to work24.1 minutes

The median value is a survey estimate, not a price for your house. A home that needs a new roof, a basement finish or an updated kitchen will sit below it, and a house in Daybreak with a lake view can sit above it.

sections.h2: Who are the largest employers in South Jordan?
sections.html:
Medical products and health care lead the list. The 2020 city financial report, as summarized on Wikipedia, ranked these employers by headcount:

  • Merit Medical, about 2,086 employees
  • Jordan School District, about 1,663
  • Ultradent, about 1,502
  • Willis Towers Watson, about 1,000
  • Walmart, about 760
  • AdvancedMD, about 655

Those numbers are two years or more old, so treat them as a rough picture. Medical manufacturing, software and education dominate the list, so the local job base leans on a few industries.

sections.h2: Which roads, rail lines and schools shape a South Jordan sale?
sections.html:
Access is strong, and buyers ask about it first. Interstate 15 runs along the eastern edge with interchanges at 10600 South and 11400 South, and Bangerter Highway crosses the middle of the city with interchanges at 9800, 10400 and 11400 South.

  • TRAX Red Line: three stations in Daybreak, at South Jordan Parkway, South Jordan Downtown and Daybreak Parkway. The ride from Daybreak Parkway to downtown Salt Lake City takes about 60 minutes.
  • FrontRunner commuter rail: a station at 10200 South.
  • Jordan School District: serves the city, including Bingham High and Herriman High, according to Wikipedia.
  • Charter and private options: Paradigm High, Early Light Academy, Hawthorne Academy, American Heritage and Stillwater Academy.

Roseman University of Health Sciences also has a campus in the city.

sections.h2: Can I rent out a South Jordan house or basement on a short-term basis?
sections.html:
Yes for some property types, no for basement apartments. South Jordan's FAQ says owners may run short-term rentals in condos, townhouses, single-family houses and guest houses, and that a guest house needs an approved accessory dwelling unit permit.

The same FAQ states that internal ADUs such as basement apartments cannot be used as short-term rentals. If your house has a finished basement that was marketed on Airbnb, a buyer's lender or inspector may ask about it, and that unit may need to be treated as a long-term rental only.

The city's business license page says licenses are not transferable under city code 5.04.100 and that you apply through its online portal. A new owner cannot simply inherit your license, so any rental income you advertise to a buyer should be described carefully.

sections.h2: Do earthquakes and radon matter when selling in South Jordan?
sections.html:
They matter at inspection time, and neither is unusual for the Wasatch Front. The Wasatch Fault runs about 240 miles through Utah, and Wikipedia reports experts estimate a 57% chance of a magnitude 6.0 or larger earthquake within 50 years. A magnitude 5.7 quake near Magna in March 2020 caused moderate damage in the valley.

Utah's radon program says one in three Utah homes has elevated radon, with 4 picocuries per liter as the action level. The state program recommends testing and suggests mitigation above that level, so a high result can add a mitigation system to the repair list.

If you sell for cash and as is, those items usually become part of the price conversation instead of a repair fight after an inspection.

sections.h2: How do property taxes work for a South Jordan seller?
sections.html:
Salt Lake County bills the tax, and the key date is November 30. The county Treasurer's calendar says that is the last day to pay current-year taxes without a penalty, and that unpaid real property taxes become delinquent on December 1.

  • Valuation notices go out by July 22, and the appeal window to the Board of Equalization runs from August 1 to September 15.
  • Tax notices are mailed by November 1.
  • A late payment carries the greater of 2.5% or $10, reduced to 1% if paid by January 31.

Utah exempts 45% of a primary residence's value, so the taxable value is 55% of market value, per the State Tax Commission. The Treasurer's office is at 2001 S State St, Suite N1-200, Salt Lake City, and its phone is (385) 468-8300. The Recorder, who files your deed, is in Suite N1-600 at (385) 468-8145.

sections.h2: How does a cash sale work in South Jordan?
sections.html:
A cash sale removes the mortgage step, so the buyer does not wait on a lender's appraisal or underwriting. You request an offer, the buyer reviews the house and the numbers, and you choose a closing date that fits your move.

The sale still closes through a title or escrow company, and the deed is recorded with the Salt Lake County Recorder. Property taxes are prorated, so the amount you owe at closing depends on how much of the year you owned the house.

Whoever buys will want to see records for the roof, the HVAC system and any finished basement, so gather those before you ask for offers.

sections.h2: What do South Jordan sellers usually run into?
sections.html:
• Unpermitted basement or garage conversions that the city does not recognize as legal units.
  • A short-term rental history that does not match the city's rules for the property type.
  • Nearby Daybreak construction that affects noise, traffic and showing schedules.
  • Elevated radon results that surface late in a financed sale.
  • A tight timeline when the seller has already bought another house.

Each of these is easier to handle when you know about it before the first showing.

faqs.q: Is South Jordan in Salt Lake County?
faqs.a: Yes. South Jordan sits entirely in Salt Lake County, so the county Assessor, Treasurer and Recorder handle your valuation, tax bill and deed. Jordan School District serves the city.

faqs.q: When are South Jordan property taxes due?
faqs.a: November 30 is the last day to pay without a penalty, according to the Salt Lake County Treasurer. Taxes unpaid on December 1 become delinquent, with a late fee that drops to 1% if you pay by January 31.

faqs.q: Can I use a basement apartment in South Jordan as an Airbnb?
faqs.a: No. The city's FAQ says internal ADUs such as basement apartments cannot be short-term rentals. Condos, townhouses, single-family houses and permitted guest houses can be, subject to the city's license rules.

faqs.q: How many people live in South Jordan?
faqs.a: The 2020 Census counted 77,487 people, up from 50,418 in 2010. Census estimates for 2020 to 2024 show about 26,740 households and an owner-occupied rate of 81.4%.

faqs.q: Can I sell a South Jordan house that needs repairs?
faqs.a: Yes. You can sell as is to a cash buyer, who prices in repairs such as an old roof or a bad basement finish. Ask for the offer in writing and compare it with what you would net after repairs and listing costs.
